name: Cross-lingual view aggregation via shared pair_id (log-prob pooling over all language/order views of a source pair)
links: Task data/ID conventions: https://inigolopezgazpio.net/SemEval-2027-Task-2-DiCo-NLI/ (final_data/*_reference.csv with reverse_pair_id); in-repo: src/labels.py (parse_instance_id, reverse_instance_id, is_flipped, REVERSE_PERM). Related prior art: test-time augmentation / multi-translation ensembling in translate-test (Ponti et al. 2021 'Modelling latent translations for cross-lingual transfer'; Artetxe et al. 2023 'Revisiting Machine Translation for Cross-lingual Classification', EMNLP, arXiv:2305.14240); Oh et al. 2022 on combining translate-train and translate-test views.
year: Technique generic (test-time view ensembling); specific to DiCo-NLI data layout, 2026
license_access: Method only, no licensing constraints; uses only official task files.
track_coverage: T4 (mixed): within-track pooling over the 6 language combinations x 2 orders of the same pair_id is available from the T4 test file alone. T1/T2/T3: within-track pooling only covers the two orders (equivalent to joint decoding); the big gain requires cross-track pooling (EN+ES+EU+mixed views of the same pair_id), which is only possible if the team submits all tracks and the test files expose a shared pair_id. Most beneficial for T3 EU and T2 ES.
basque_quality: Largest beneficiary: EU predictions borrow evidence from the EN view (where DeBERTa-style models are strongest, pilot 0.75 W-F1) and from ES. Effectively a translate-test using the organizers' human-verified translations rather than MT, which avoids MT errors on short phrases. No published numbers; expected EU W-F1 to approach the EN level [uncertain].
cross_lingual_robustness: By construction all views of a pair receive the same (orientation-adjusted) label, so the monolingual-vs-mixed gap collapses to zero at the prediction level; the remaining error is the error of the pooled estimate. The flip side: when pooled evidence is wrong, all views across all tracks are wrong together (correlated errors), and if a translation genuinely changes the relation for a given language (items the organizers failed to filter), pooling forces a wrong label on that view [uncertain].
architecture: Inference-time aggregation. For every test instance parse (pair_id, lang1, lang2, direction). Get 4-way log-probs from one or more models for every view v of pair_id (up to 18 views for a reversible pair: 3 monolingual x 2 orders + 6 mixed combos x 2 orders; NEG singletons have fewer). Map each view into the canonical 'original' orientation: if is_flipped(v), lp_v = lp_v[REVERSE_PERM]. Pool: s = sum_v w_v * lp_v (weights per language/combination tuned on dev, e.g. higher for EN views and for stronger models). Decide the canonical label y* = argmax s (optionally with a tuned NEG bias), then emit y* for original views and Rev(y*) for flipped views. Variants: product-of-experts (sum log-probs), mean of probabilities, or two-stage (pool NEG gate across views, then direction). Subsumes joint pair decoding within each track.
params: None beyond the underlying models (a handful of pooling weights / one NEG bias tuned on dev).
compute: Negligible: a groupby over pair_id on stored probability arrays; runs on CPU in seconds. Requires the underlying model(s) to have scored every view, i.e. running inference on all four tracks' test files (~4k rows per monolingual track, T4 roughly 6x that if the train ratio holds).
sample_efficiency: Not trained (except a few weights), so no small-data issue; pooling up to 18 correlated views reduces variance of the decision, which also reduces seed variance of the final submission. Pooling weights and NEG bias should be tuned with grouped CV on train+dev to avoid overfitting 660-row dev files.
reported_results: No direct literature numbers for this exact setting. Analogous evidence: ensembling multiple translations / views improves cross-lingual classification (Ponti et al. 2021 latent-translation ensembling; Artetxe et al. 2023 show translate-test with a strong English model reaching 85.9-86.7 XNLI vs 84.3 for XLM-R translate-train, i.e. routing non-English inputs through the English view is strong). XNLIeu (Heredia et al. 2024) shows a ~2.7-point gap between EN-derived translate-train (83.8) and zero-shot (81.1) for XLM-R-large on Basque; pooling with human-verified EN views should exceed both since it uses the gold source-language text [uncertain].
pilot_dico_results: Not evaluated in the LREC 2026 pilot (English-only, no multilingual tracks).
negative_other_handling: NEG is pooled like any other class (NEG maps to itself under REVERSE_PERM), so all views of a pair share one NEG/non-NEG decision; a pooled NEG bias/threshold is tuned on dev for weighted F1. Yes, it can emit NEG on a gold-reversible pair, but then consistently for every view and both orders. Note: in train/dev NEG items are singletons per language combination (no reversed twin), so a pair_id whose views never include a flipped twin is itself a strong NEG signal; that singleton cue is a separate, riskier heuristic (see structural-cue item) and should not be folded in silently.
metric_tradeoff: SoftCons: 1.0 on pairs predicted reversible (same guarantee as joint decoding). HardCons and W-F1: expected to improve on ES/EU/mixed because weaker views inherit the stronger EN evidence and variance is reduced; on T1 EN, cross-track pooling may give a small gain or small loss (ES/EU views are noisier than EN; mitigate by weighting EN views higher). Because all views share one decision, per-pair errors become fully correlated across tracks, increasing variance of the aggregate score across test samples but not its expectation.
integration: Post-processing script operating on per-track prediction files with probabilities: load all tracks, parse instance_id with src/labels.py, canonicalise with REVERSE_PERM for flipped views, groupby pair_id, pool, then write per-track submission CSVs (instance_id,label) with Rev applied to flipped rows. Keep a switch for within-track-only pooling (rule-safe mode) vs cross-track pooling.
ensemble_compatibility: Native: it is itself an ensemble over views and can also pool over multiple models/seeds/folds in the same sum. Needs calibrated per-class probabilities (temperature-scale each model on dev before pooling).
inference_cost: Cost of scoring all views once (all four test files) plus a trivial CPU pooling step; minutes on a single GPU for encoder backbones.
rules_disclosure: Must be disclosed explicitly. Within-track pooling (orders and, for T4, the 6 language combinations in the same file) uses only that track's test input and is low risk. Cross-track pooling uses test inputs of other tracks (e.g. the English phrase for a Basque test item), which arguably turns T3 'Basque NLI' into English NLI on human translations; the organizers describe the monolingual tracks as independent and plan split grouping to prevent cross-lingual leakage, so this could be judged against the spirit of the tracks or explicitly banned in final rules. Ask the organizers before submitting cross-track pooled runs, and report it as system metadata (hybrid/ensemble, uses cross-track test inputs) [uncertain].
contamination: No external data and no train/test leakage (splits are grouped by source pair across all tracks and languages). The only concern is the rules/spirit issue of cross-track test-input sharing, not contamination.
structural_cue_dependence: High. Relies on pair_id being shared and visible across views/tracks and on the instance_id format <pair_id>__<l1>-<l2>__<original|flipped> in the test release. If test ids are anonymised or scrambled, cross-view grouping would need to be reconstructed by content matching (possible for within-track twins by swapping phrases, much harder across languages) [uncertain whether test ids keep this format].
priority: P0 for within-track pooling (orders + T4 language combinations: safe, cheap, strong for T4); P1 for cross-track pooling pending organizer clarification of the rules.
expected_gain: Within-track: SoftCons to ~1.0 (as joint decoding) and for T4 +2-5 W-F1 / HardCons from averaging 6 language combinations [uncertain]. Cross-track: T3 EU and T2 ES W-F1/HardCons could rise by several points toward the EN level (+3-8 [uncertain]), T1 EN roughly neutral (+-1). Gains are largest when the per-view models are diverse but individually calibrated.
